options: The formal document that authorizes a governance program, naming its purpose, scope, sponsor, and success criteria
A slide deck used only for the kickoff meeting
A technical specification for a data warehouse
A list of software vendors being evaluated
questions.explain: The charter is the reference document the program points back to for its authority, scope, and goals — not a one-time presentation.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what is the single most common reason governance programs fail?
options: Scope that tries to cover all enterprise data at once instead of a phased, named scope
Choosing the wrong database vendor
Having too many stewards
Writing the charter in business language instead of technical language
questions.explain: A charter with no boundaries gives the program no way to ever declare success or prioritize work — the lesson's central scope warning.

questions.q: In a phased scope statement, what should phase one explicitly include?
options: A list of what is out of scope for now, in addition to what is in scope
Every data domain in the company, governed simultaneously
Only the IT department's systems
A ban on adding any domain later
questions.explain: Writing down what's explicitly out of scope for now keeps the charter honest and prevents stakeholders from assuming the program owns problems it hasn't reached yet.

questions.q: Who typically drafts the program charter, and who approves it?
options: The executive sponsor and program lead draft it together; the governance council or committee approves it
A single IT administrator drafts and approves it alone
An outside auditor drafts and approves it
It requires no approval once it is written
questions.explain: The sponsor brings authority and the program lead brings operational detail; formal approval comes from the governance body described in Foundations Lesson 16.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say a charter needs a named executive sponsor?
options: Without named authority backing it, the charter carries no more weight than an email and can be cancelled by any reorg
Sponsors are required by law in every industry
The sponsor is the person who writes all the governance policies personally
A sponsor's only role is to approve the program's budget
questions.explain: The charter's authority comes from the sponsor's backing — without it, nothing written down says the program is supposed to exist.
